cd /hutian/wiki/w && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='Outline.md'
s=open(p).read()
L=s.split('\n'); out=[]
for l in L:
    if l.startswith('- **M5 as reported:**'):
        l=("- **M5 as reported (rev 7, `mstar_tobit.csv`, replaces the interpolated −1.07):** slope of φ-error vs m ≈ −0.5 for the unbiased paired estimator (estimator check passes); shap `num_features(10)` ≈ 0 in φ-error (biased, does not converge: share 0.68–0.87 at default). The m*(g) relation is now decided by `analysis`'s interval-censored (Tobit) regression of log m* on log margin, instance-bootstrap CI: at d ≥ 16 exact top-3 slope **−1.4 to −1.8 for `kernel_paired`** (German MLP −1.78 [−2.03, −1.60], ACS-Employment RF −1.58 [−1.73, −1.45]) and **−1.7 to −2.1 for antithetic permutation** (−2 inside the CI in 6 of 7 cells); the earlier −1.07 excluded censored instances and was biased flat. For shap's own `l1_reg=False` the slope is shallower (−0.8 to −1.2 on German/ACS-Employment MLP/RF/GBM; LR ≈ 0 because it is deterministic). 8–29 of 40–60 instances are right-censored for `kernel_paired`, so the fit rests on the Gaussian-residual assumption; at d ≤ 10 (Pima, GMSC; ≥ 90% censored) it is uninformative. For P_c^ε(0.05) m* hardly depends on the margin (slope ≈ 0 to −0.3). **Statement the paper makes:** m* falls roughly like g^−1.5…−2 for the unbiased samplers, \"not confirmed as exactly −2\"; no refutation claim. The per-instance probit on g√m/σ_k with collapse (idea-review #6.4) remains a robustness check I asked for; the Tobit fit is accepted as the primary M5 estimate (claim owner's decision), and the paper says it assumes Gaussian residuals under heavy right-censoring.")
    if l.startswith('- **The value function is less stable than the run, at B=50'):
        l=l+("\n  - *rev 7, partial B-sensitivity (`background_reference_shift.csv`; German, ACS-Employment, up to 30 instances, German RF n=9–10):* the exact top-3 set of the B=50 reference stays the same under B=20 for 23–47%, under k-means-50 for 50–89%, under B=200 for 46–100% of instances. So the reference's top-3 depends on the background draw even at B=200 against B=50, and it moves toward stability with B but does not settle; this is *not yet* the floor-b-vs-B curve (that needs two independent draws at each B, same instances as floor a), so the paper still says \"at B=50\" and presents these as reference shifts, with n. **German MLP retraining floors are unusable** (AUC filter kept 1/24 bootstrap and 3/24 hyperparameter retrainings; only `c_seed` kept 6/15): the paper shows floor c for German MLP as not available, not as a number.")
    out.append(l)
s='\n'.join(out)
s=s.replace("- rev 6 (issue #6,","- rev 7 (`analysis`'s update on #5): M5 decided by the Tobit fit (m* slope −1.4…−1.8 paired, −1.7…−2.1 permutation; not confirmed as exactly −2, not refuted); partial background reference shifts added; German MLP retrain floor unusable.\n- rev 6 (issue #6,",1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

shown.message:
Outline rev 7 is pushed. It updates the story from `experiment-repo`'s latest tables.

- **M5:** `experiment-repo` corrected its own earlier slope of −1.07, which came from dropping the censored instances. The interval-censored (Tobit) fit gives these slopes for the minimum budget against the margin at d ≥ 16.

  | Sampler | Slope | Note |
  |---|---|---|
  | Paired Kernel SHAP | −1.4 to −1.8 | |
  | Antithetic permutation | −1.7 to −2.1 | −2 inside the CI in 6 of 7 cells |
  | shap's own `l1_reg=False` | −0.8 to −1.2 | shallower |

  8–29 of 40–60 instances are right-censored for the paired sampler, so the fit rests on a Gaussian-residual assumption. The paper will say "not confirmed as exactly −2", and will not call it refuted. I accepted the Tobit fit as the main M5 estimate. The probit check that `idea-review` asked for stays as a robustness item that does not block anything.
- **Background:** the exact top-3 set at B=50 stays the same under B=20 for 23–47% of instances, under k-means-50 for 50–89%, and under B=200 for 46–100%. Samples are small: up to 30 instances, and 9–10 for German RF. These compare each background against one B=50 draw, so they are reference shifts and not yet the floor-b-against-B curve. The paper keeps saying "at B=50". I asked `experiment-repo` for two independent draws at B=20 and B=200 on the same instances as floor a.
- **German MLP retrain floor:** unusable. The AUC filter kept 1 of 24 bootstrap and 3 of 24 hyperparameter retrainings, so the paper reports it as not available.
